title: The 1962 Alcatraz escape — three men who vanished
sources: Wikipedia: June 1962 Alcatraz escape — on the night of 11 June 1962 Frank Morris and brothers John and Clarence Anglin escaped from Alcatraz; over six months they widened the ventilation ducts beneath their sinks with discarded saw blades, mess-hall spoons and a drill improvised from a vacuum-cleaner motor, hid the work with painted cardboard and masked the noise with Morris's accordion during music hour; on the vacant top level of the cellblock they built life preservers and a raft from more than fifty raincoats; dummy heads of soap, toothpaste, concrete dust and toilet paper, painted and topped with hair from the barbershop floor, lay in their beds; a fourth man, Allen West, was left behind when his vent opening had hardened too narrow; the three climbed a ventilation shaft to the roof, slid 50 ft down a kitchen vent pipe, climbed two barbed-wire fences and launched the raft at about 10 pm; the escape was discovered at 7 am on 12 June when Clarence Anglin's dummy head fell to the floor as guards tried to rouse him; a paddle, a plastic-wrapped wallet with Anglin family photos and life vests were found; the FBI concluded in 1979 that they most likely drowned; family members presented evidence they reached Brazil; in 2013 San Francisco police received a letter claiming to be from John Anglin, whose authenticity was deemed inconclusive; in November 2025 a team rebuilt the raft from the same plans and showed the crossing was plausible

Photos (public domain, Wikimedia Commons / FBI / US Bureau of Prisons / Historic American Buildings Survey / Library of Congress, Carol M. Highsmith): the dummy head from Frank Morris's cell (FBI, 1962); John Anglin's Alcatraz mugshot; the Alcatraz cell house and cells; aerial views of Alcatraz Island; the Golden Gate and Angel Island
Archive film (public domain): Golden Gate Bridge opening (1936); US Navy footage of night at sea (1943) — illustrative
Music: Grieg, In the Hall of the Mountain King — Musopen Symphony, public domain

post.facebook:
On the morning of 12 June 1962, a guard at Alcatraz tried to wake a prisoner. His head rolled onto the floor.

It was fake — soap, toilet paper and real hair from the prison barbershop. Three men were gone: Frank Morris and the brothers John and Clarence Anglin.

For six months they had dug through the walls under their sinks with spoons and a drill made from a vacuum cleaner, while Morris played the accordion during music hour to cover the noise. On the empty top floor of the cell block they built a raft from more than fifty stolen raincoats. On the night of 11 June they climbed to the roof, slid down a pipe, got over two fences and pushed their raft into the dark bay. A fourth man was left behind — his hole was too small.

Searchers found a paddle, a life vest and a wallet wrapped in plastic — never the men. The FBI decided they drowned; their family says they made it to Brazil. In 2013 police received a letter signed "John Anglin" saying he was alive — never proven. And in 2025 a team rebuilt their raft from the same plans and made it across.

Drowned in the bay — or the perfect escape? 👇
